The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 16.2.2019 at about 11.15 a.m. the petitioner was pedestrian proceeding in front of Mysore Food Palace, Modi Hospital Road, Bengaluru, at that time, one motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JT-4111 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Prestine Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.
She was discharged with an advise of follow-up treatment and had spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards her medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment.

2 4 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 4.

It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner hale, healthy and was working as a Tax Analyst and getting salary of Rs.45,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, she could not able to do any work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JT-4111.
In this regard, case was registered against the rider of offending vehicle by the jurisdictional Vijayanagar Traffic Police, in Crime No.23/2019.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.

6. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared through their respective counsel, the respondent No.1 & 2 have not filed their written statements, on the other hand, the respondent No.3 has filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.3, it is contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further it has denied the manner in which the 5 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 accident took place, injuries sustained, avocation, age and income of the petitioner and also expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.
The respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defense of the respondent No.3 that there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JT-4111.
It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner herself.
Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
It is also the contention of the respondent No.3 that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken 6 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 place on 16.2.2019 at about 11.15 a.m. infront of Mysore Food Palace, Mode Hospital Road, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JT-4111 in an actionable negligence?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to P14.

11.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the materials available on record.

12. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-

13. It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02- JT-4111, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.3, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
15. The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
PW1 in her examination- in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P9
. Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.23/2019 of Vijayanagar Traffic Police Station, 8 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 Ex

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Vijayanagar Traffic Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC and section 134(a & b) R/W 187 of IMV Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and section 134(a & b) R/W 187 of IMV Act.

On the contrary, the respondent No.3 examined authorised investigator as RW1.
He has deposed in his evidence that, after procuring the crime records, he had visited the petitioner to 9 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 ascertain the details of the alleged accident.

As per the statement of the petitioner the accident was on account of rider of the motor cycle by college student along with pillion rider, who also happens to be the student and was not holding driving licence and the petitioner is the son of the owner of the motor cycle and had shared the CCTV footage of live accident.

Further deposed that thereafter, he had visited the place of owner and learnt that the charge sheeted rider is not his son but far relative, the owner swapped the name of the rider and got the charge sheet filed in the name of Mohammed Younis Pasha.
The insured knowingly fully well that he has handed over the person who was not holding driving licence to ride the motor cycle in contravention with the policy terms and conditions.
He has placed authorisation letter, investigation report, CD and report pertaining to CD.

As per Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
18.

In this regard, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, it shows that, after investigation I.O. has filed the charge sheet against the driver Mohammed Younis Pasha @ Mohammed Younis Pasha.

sentences.text: To disprove the contents of the charge sheet, no supportive evidence is 10 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P8.
Further Ex.P5 is the notice u/s 133 of MV Act issued by the Investigating officer to the owner of the offending vehicle to produce relevant documents.

In answer to the Ex.P5, owner of the offending vehicle had given reply as per Ex.P6, in the said document, in the column driver name and address clearly mentioned as Mohammed Yonus Pasha Son of Mohammed Ismail Sab.

Even in Ex.P10 &
Ex.P11- order sheet in CC 2250/2019 & Judgment copy in CC 2250/2019, the name of the accused is mentioned as Mohammed Younis Pasha.
Further in Ex.P12-evidence of the petitioner in CC 2250/2019 shows she has identified the rider of the offending vehicle.
Though the judgment of the criminal court is not binding on the tribunal, but it has to be considered other facts and circumstances.

Moreover, the respondent No.3 has not made an effort to examine the rider of the offending vehicle to eradicate all the allegations to prove that as on the date of the accident Mohammed Younis Pasha was not the rider of the offending vehicle.
Added to this, the CD as per Ex.R3 produced by the respondent is not playing.
Further if the rider was different person, what prevented the respondent No.3 to produce the 11 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 CCTV footage before the I.O.
The respondent No.3 has not challenged Ex.P10 to Ex.P12 and Ex.P18 charge sheet filed against Mohammed Yunus of the offending vehicle.

All these facts and circumstances clearly reflects that the respondent No.3 has failed to establish that as on the date of the accident Mohammed Younis Pasha was not the rider of the offending vehicle.

19. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.3 about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Even at the time of cross- examination of RW1 he has stated that he does not know the accident personally and giving evidence on the basis of documents.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JT-4111.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.

Hence, without 12 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 making much Neha.R vs Mohammed Younis Pasha on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117126125/
5 discussion on the point of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

22. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation 13 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P9.

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Laceration over dorsum of left foot measuring 10 cm X 7x 1cm with dorsal skin degloving and tenderness over left foot.
2) Abrasion over right and left wrist each measuring 3 cm X 2 cm 14 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 3) Abrasion over upper lip measuirng 2 cmx 1 cm.

Neha. R vs Mohammed Younis Pasha on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117126125/
6 24.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature and the injury No.2 & 3 are simple in nature.
Further, the petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
On perusal of wound certificate reveals that the petitoner was admitted on 16.2.2019 and discharged on 20.2.2019.
Further she has placed x-rays as per Ex.P13.
Except production of these documents she has not placed any documents to show the mode of treatment.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
25.
PW1 has stated that, she was working as a Tax Analyst at Ernst and Young Company and drawing salary of Rs.45,000/- per month.
She has not placed any documents to show that she was 15 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
Moreover, she has not placed leave sanction letter to show that how many days she took the leave due to the accidental injuries.
On going through the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 16.2.2019 and discharged on 20.2.2019.
During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.19,205/- as per Ex.P14.
There are no contra materials available on record to show prove that the medical bills are created and fabricated.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.19,205/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge 16 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 summaries the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient and also as an outpatient.
During that period, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, she had sustained grievous injuries, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.

Except the production of medical documents and averments made in the main petition as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor,
in order to prove the disability sustained by her, due to the accidental injuries in order to know,
whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner will effect to her future and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort to the petitioner to do her routine work as well as her work for her avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner.
Further the petitioner has 17 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 continued her service as usual.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future income due to want of evidence on record.

Loss of amenities;
29.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that due to the accidental injuries, petitioner suffered great untold hardship, mental shock and agony.
On perusal of evidence of PW1 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.2,000/- towards loss of amenities.
30. In connection with the future medication, the petitioner has not stated about future medication.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation of under the head of future medical expenses.

31. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
18 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs.20,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 5,000-00 laid-up period and rest period
3. Medical expenses Rs.19,205-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 4,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income NIL due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 2,000-00 7.
Future medication NIL Total Rs.50,205-00 32.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,205/- (Rupees fifty thousand two hundred and five only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

19 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 LIABILITY:
33.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JT-4111, alleged accident had taken place.

The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
34.
The respondent No.3 has admitted bout issuance of insurance policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-JT-4111 and its validity.

As such, I am of the view that,
the respondent No.3 being insurance company and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is the rider of the motor cycle, he is acted according to his master's instruction.
Hence, the petition against the respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

20 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 ISSUE No.3:
35.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.2 & 3 is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.50,205/- (Rupees fifty thousand two hundred and five only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 & 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation with 21 SCCH-18 MVC No.3069/2020 interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the amount is very meagre entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
